what_it_shows: Percent of the 219 countries and territories missing each core column in each year 2000-2021, marking the 2017 producer-data break and the end of GDP after 2018.
why_this_chart: A column-by-year heatmap shows the structure of missingness (whole blocks versus scattered cells) for every variable at once, which a table of ~400 numbers cannot.

what_it_shows: World electricity generation by source 2000-2021, summed over a fixed panel of countries, with the fossil/low-carbon boundary and the low-carbon share.
why_this_chart: A stacked area shows both the total and each source's contribution over time, so growth in total demand and the shift between sources are visible in one view.

what_it_shows: Histograms of energy, GDP and electricity per person and grid carbon intensity across countries in 2018, on raw scales, with median and skewness.
why_this_chart: Histograms show the shape of each distribution (skew, long tails, outliers), which decides whether raw scales are suitable for distance-based models and OLS.

what_it_shows: GDP per person vs primary energy per person in 2018 on linear axes, bubble area = population; top-10 energy users and the 3 most populous countries labelled.
why_this_chart: A scatter is the standard view of a relationship between two quantities; bubble size adds population, so the reader sees that the axes are set by a few small states while most people live in the crowded bottom-left corner.

what_it_shows: Pearson and Spearman correlation matrices of 7 key variables in 2018 (same countries), with cells where the two differ by at least 0.2 outlined.
why_this_chart: Side-by-side annotated heatmaps make the two coefficient matrices directly comparable cell by cell; outlining large gaps points to non-linearity and outliers.

what_it_shows: Share of each country's electricity from nuclear and renewables in 2018, on a fixed 0-100% scale; excluded countries in grey.
why_this_chart: A choropleth shows the spatial pattern of the energy transition (regional clusters such as hydro-rich South America and fossil-based Middle East) that a table or bar chart would hide.

what_it_shows: Each country's change in low-carbon electricity share between 2000-02 and 2016-18 (histogram, with the +/- threshold for a large change) and its rank at both endpoints (rank-rank scatter), top movers labelled.
why_this_chart: The histogram shows how large changes are and in which direction; the rank-rank scatter shows whether countries keep their positions (diagonal) or overtake each other, which is exactly what a single-year snapshot cannot show.

what_it_shows: Residuals against fitted values for the raw-scale OLS of energy per person on GDP per person (2018), with a LOWESS trend and the 5 largest residuals labelled.
why_this_chart: The residual-vs-fitted plot is the standard regression diagnostic: a funnel shows heteroscedasticity and a curved trend shows non-linearity, both of which a single R-squared hides.

what_it_shows: K-means inertia (elbow) and mean silhouette for k = 2..8 on the standardised 2018 mix shares and intensities, with the k chosen by the pre-set rule marked.
why_this_chart: Line charts over k are the standard way to compare cluster counts; showing the elbow and the silhouette side by side, with silhouette strength bands shaded, makes the choice of k checkable instead of a judgement call.

what_it_shows: Countries on the first two principal components of the iteration 1 clustering features, coloured by K-means cluster, next to a correlation circle of the feature loadings.
why_this_chart: A PCA biplot is the usual way to see 11-dimensional clusters in 2-D and to read which features separate them; splitting points and arrows into two panels with the same axes keeps both readable.

what_it_shows: Each country's iteration 1 K-means cluster (k = 8) on a world map.
why_this_chart: A categorical choropleth shows whether clusters follow geography (regional resource endowments) or cut across it, which a scatter plot cannot show.

what_it_shows: Out-of-fold Random Forest predictions of 2018 grid carbon intensity against the actual values, with the 1:1 line, the mean-predictor baseline, cross-validated metrics and the 8 largest errors named; colour = dominant source (display only).
why_this_chart: A predicted-vs-actual scatter shows both overall fit (distance from the 1:1 line) and which countries fail; colouring by a variable the model never saw reveals systematic error that one R-squared value hides.

what_it_shows: Permutation importance of each Random Forest feature on held-out folds: the mean rise in MAE (gCO2/kWh) when the feature is shuffled, with ±1 sd whiskers.
why_this_chart: Sorted horizontal bars compare a handful of features on one scale and leave room for long names; the error bars show whether an importance is distinguishable from 0.

what_it_shows: Out-of-fold Random Forest residual (actual minus predicted carbon intensity, 2018) for each of the countries in the RF set, on a diverging scale centred at 0.
why_this_chart: A diverging choropleth centred at zero shows whether errors cluster in space (e.g. hydro-rich regions under one colour), which a residual table cannot show.

what_it_shows: Before/after table of the feedback loop: unit of analysis, rows, years, feature columns, scale, mix representation, income context and time information, each linked to the iteration 1 inference that triggered it.
why_this_chart: A two-column table states exactly what changed in the data, with computed counts; it is the clearest proof that the loop transformed the data rather than restyled it.

what_it_shows: Histograms of energy, electricity and GDP per person in 2018, raw (top) and after log1p (bottom), with n and skewness from results/loop_skew.csv.
why_this_chart: Paired histograms on the same countries show the shape change directly: a long right tail on the raw scale becomes a roughly symmetric distribution after log1p.

what_it_shows: PCA of the 2018 electricity mix for the iteration 2 countries: z-scored raw shares (left) vs CLR log-ratios (right), coloured by dominant source, with the pair whose distance rank rises most joined in both panels.
why_this_chart: Side-by-side PCA scatters of the same countries show how the representation changes the geometry: which countries are neighbours, and how much variance the first two components hold.

what_it_shows: Each country's yearly growth of GDP per person vs energy use per person (2000-02 to 2016-18), with the 45-degree and zero lines, the decoupling classes and their counts; colour = data-derived income tier, hollow = small state.
why_this_chart: A growth-vs-growth scatter turns decoupling into geometry: the 45-degree line separates relative decoupling from coupling and the zero line marks absolute decoupling, so the class of every country is visible at once.

what_it_shows: Energy vs GDP per person (2018) on log-log axes with the OLS fit, its HC3 95% confidence band, the elasticity with CI, R-squared and Breusch-Pagan p; the largest residuals are named.
why_this_chart: Log axes turn a multiplicative relationship into a straight line whose slope is the elasticity, and spread the countries that crowded the corner of the raw-scale plot.

what_it_shows: Decoupling (GDP growth minus energy growth, pp per year) per income tier: box plot plus every country, n per tier, the Kruskal-Wallis p and the Holm-corrected pairs that differ.
why_this_chart: A box plot with the points overlaid shows each tier's median and spread and every country behind it, which matters with ~40 countries per tier; the test results sit on the same figure.

what_it_shows: Median low-carbon share of electricity per income tier in 2000-02 and 2019-21, with the interquartile range at each end and the median per-country change.
why_this_chart: A slope chart compares four groups at two time points with one line each: the direction and steepness of each line is the tier's change, and crossings are immediately visible.

what_it_shows: K-means inertia and silhouette and diagonal-GMM BIC and silhouette for k = 3..7 on the archetype matrix; circled points have a cluster under 5 countries.
why_this_chart: Small multiples put the four model-selection criteria on one k axis, so the choice follows the documented rule rather than one favourite curve.

what_it_shows: Mean silhouette of K-means on the same 152 countries in the iteration 1 feature space (at k = 8 and at the iteration 2 k) and in the iteration 2 space.
why_this_chart: A bar per feature space on one axis answers a single question: did the transformation make clusters better separated? Reference lines mark the Kaufman-Rousseeuw cut-offs.

what_it_shows: Standardised centroid of every archetype on the 9 trajectory and 8 CLR features.
why_this_chart: A diverging heatmap centred at 0 shows at a glance which features separate which archetype, and the black line splits trajectory features from mix features.

what_it_shows: Archetype of every country in the iteration 2 set (small states assigned post hoc).
why_this_chart: A categorical choropleth checks whether the archetypes are geographic blocs or cut across regions, which the heatmap cannot show.

what_it_shows: Median and interquartile band of the low-carbon share of electricity, 2000-2021, per archetype.
why_this_chart: One panel per archetype on a shared y axis shows each group's path without the overplotting of 160 lines, and makes levels directly comparable.

what_it_shows: Grid carbon intensity in 2018 for fossil producers (production >= own energy use, 2000-16 means) and all other countries, with the Mann-Whitney test.
why_this_chart: A box plot with every country overlaid compares two groups' medians and spreads and shows the exceptions (clean-grid producers) that a bar of means would hide.

what_it_shows: Cross-validated R² and MAE of the mean predictor, RF v1 and RF v2 on the same countries and folds (bars = mean, whiskers = fold sd, lines = paired folds).
why_this_chart: Bars with fold error bars show the size of the change against fold-to-fold noise, and the paired lines show whether v2 wins consistently or only on average.

what_it_shows: Held-out permutation importance of every RF v2 feature (rise in MAE when shuffled).
why_this_chart: A sorted horizontal bar chart ranks features and its error bars show which importances are distinguishable from zero; colour marks the features the loop added.
